```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

`specshiny` v0.4.0 introduces three practitioner-oriented capabilities built on
top of the same schema-validated IR (`spec_ir` v1.2.0) and AST-verified
compilation pipeline:

1. **Longitudinal growth-curve designs** (`design_type = "longitudinal_growth"`)
   with explicit wave schedules (`time_points`, `time_spacing`), random
   intercepts and random time slopes, stationary within-subject AR(1) residual
   autocorrelation (`outcome$ar1_rho`), and strictly monotone post-baseline
   dropout (`missingness$mechanism = "monotone_dropout"`).
2. **Multi-scenario design comparison** (`compare_specs()`) quantifying total
   sample size $N$, cluster design effect ($\mathrm{DEFF}$), effective sample
   size ($N_{\mathrm{eff}}$), variance decomposition, semantic IR diffs, and
   optional comparative Monte Carlo power.
3. **An extensible domain template registry** (`list_spec_templates()`,
   `use_spec_template()`, `register_spec_template()`,
   `unregister_spec_template()`) that gates every registered template through
   both `assert_valid_spec_ir()` and `verify_compiled_r_ast()`.

```{r setup}
library(specshiny)
```

## 1. Longitudinal Growth Curves with AR(1) & Monotone Dropout

Plain-English descriptions of repeated-measures growth studies compile directly
into `spec_ir` v1.2.0 using the offline `translator_rule()` backend:

```{r nl-longitudinal}
prompt <- paste(
  "Longitudinal growth curve simulation with 120 subjects across 5 waves,",
  "ICC 0.4, AR(1) correlation 0.4, growth slope 0.35, random slope for time,",
  "treatment effect 0.25, 25% monotone dropout, 200 replications"
)

tr <- nl_to_spec(prompt)
tr$spec
```

Refinements update wave counts, time schedules, autocorrelation, and dropout
rates while maintaining all statistical sanity guardrails (such as keeping
`abs(ar1_rho) < 0.95` and synchronizing `time_points`, `cluster_size`, and
`time_spacing`):

```{r refine-longitudinal}
ref <- refine_spec(tr$spec, "increase to 6 waves and set AR(1) rho to 0.55")
ref$diff
spec_to_math(ref$spec)$latex
```

Notice that `spec_to_controls()` synthesizes longitudinal-specific controls
(`time_points`, `ar1_rho`, and `"monotone_dropout"` in the missingness
selector) while omitting inapplicable cross-sectional cluster-size distribution
widgets:

```{r controls-longitudinal}
desc <- spec_to_controls(ref$spec)
desc$sections$hierarchy$controls[[2]]$id
desc$sections$outcome$controls[[4]]$id
desc$available_grid_axes
```

### Compiling and Verifying AR(1) & Monotone Dropout Behavior

`compile_r_script()` deterministically emits standalone R code (verified via
`verify_compiled_r_ast(strict = TRUE)`) implementing stationary AR(1) within-
subject innovations and strictly monotone wave-by-wave attrition:

```{r execute-longitudinal}
sp_demo <- use_spec_template(
  "longitudinal_growth_ar1",
  n_clusters = 150L,
  ar1_rho = 0.50,
  n_reps = 2L
)

r_script <- compile_r_script(sp_demo)
ast_report <- verify_compiled_r_ast(r_script)
c(ast_safe = ast_report$safe, expressions = ast_report$n_expressions)

# Source the compiled script in an isolated environment and inspect one draw
f_tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
writeLines(r_script, f_tmp)
sim_env <- new.env(parent = baseenv())
invisible(capture.output(sys.source(f_tmp, envir = sim_env)))
unlink(f_tmp)

dat <- sim_env$simulate_one_dataset(sim_env$cfg)
miss_mat <- matrix(is.na(dat$y), nrow = sp_demo$hierarchy$n_clusters,
                   ncol = sp_demo$hierarchy$time_points, byrow = TRUE)

c(
  wave1_missing = sum(miss_mat[, 1L]),
  all_subjects_strictly_monotone = all(apply(miss_mat, 1L, function(r) all(diff(as.integer(r)) >= 0L))),
  final_wave_dropout_rate = round(mean(miss_mat[, ncol(miss_mat)]), 3)
)
```

## 2. Comparing Competing Designs with `compare_specs()`

When designing a study, researchers routinely trade off sample size, cluster
allocation, cluster-size imbalance, and repeated-measures structure.
`compare_specs()` evaluates two or more validated `spec_ir` objects side by
side using the Kish / Eldridge-Ashby-Kerry design effect:

$$\mathrm{DEFF} = 1 + \left(\bar{n}_j (1 + \mathrm{CV}^2) - 1\right)\mathrm{ICC},
\qquad N_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{N}{\mathrm{DEFF}}.$$

```{r compare-designs}
s_ols  <- use_spec_template("factorial_ols", n_obs = 400L)
s_crt  <- use_spec_template("cluster_rct", n_clusters = 40L, cluster_size = 10L)
s_mlm  <- use_spec_template("cross_level_mlm", n_clusters = 40L, cluster_size = 10L, cluster_size_sd = 4)
s_long <- use_spec_template("longitudinal_growth_ar1", n_clusters = 80L, ar1_rho = 0.45)

cmp <- compare_specs(
  ols = s_ols,
  balanced_crt = s_crt,
  unbalanced_mlm = s_mlm,
  longitudinal_ar1 = s_long
)

cmp
```

Extract the full comparison table with `as.data.frame()` or examine metric
deltas relative to the baseline scenario:

```{r compare-df}
as.data.frame(cmp)[, c("scenario", "total_n", "cluster_size_cv", "icc", "deff", "n_eff", "n_controls")]
cmp$deltas
```

Setting `run_power = TRUE` runs a bounded pure-R preview simulation for every
scenario under a shared random seed so you can inspect comparative power, bias,
and standard errors alongside analytical efficiency:

```{r compare-power}
cmp_pwr <- compare_specs(
  ols = s_ols,
  balanced_crt = s_crt,
  run_power = TRUE,
  preview_reps = 10L,
  seed = 2026L
)
as.data.frame(cmp_pwr)[, c("scenario", "total_n", "n_eff", "focal_effect", "est_power", "est_mean_se")]
```

## 3. Built-In & Custom Domain Templates

`specshiny` ships five immutable built-in templates spanning experimental,
multilevel, longitudinal, and generalized linear designs:

```{r list-templates}
list_spec_templates()[, c("name", "source", "category", "design_type", "estimator")]
```

Instantiate any template with parameter overrides (by control ID, shorthand
field name, or dotted IR path) and optional natural-language refinement:

```{r use-template}
s_custom <- use_spec_template(
  "longitudinal_growth_ar1",
  overrides = list("outcome.ar1_rho" = 0.60, title = "Quarterly Clinical Trial"),
  time_spacing = c(0, 3, 6, 9, 12),
  n_clusters = 100L,
  refine = "add 20% monotone dropout"
)
s_custom
```

Teams can register their own reusable templates with `register_spec_template()`.
Registration is strictly gated by both `assert_valid_spec_ir()` and
`verify_compiled_r_ast(compile_r_script(spec), strict = TRUE)`, so invalid or
unsafe specifications can never enter the registry:

```{r register-template}
register_spec_template(
  name = "quarterly_clinical_growth",
  spec = s_custom,
  description = "5-wave quarterly growth curve with AR(1) rho = 0.60 and 20% monotone dropout.",
  category = "clinical"
)

list_spec_templates(category = "clinical")[, c("name", "source", "category", "design_type")]

# Instantiate directly from the custom template
s_run <- use_spec_template("quarterly_clinical_growth", n_clusters = 140L)
spec_total_n(s_run)

# Clean up session registry
unregister_spec_template("quarterly_clinical_growth")
```
